title: The Singing Genealogy Where Each Cell Hears Its Own Making

features.name: genealogy tower
features.desc-on-touch: You follow stacked hexagons upward, each carved with a mother-line going back. The tower hums—three hundred queens in ascending echo.

features.name: singing line
features.desc-on-touch: Six dancers hold bells tuned to their bloodlines. When they move, their bells carry the sound of who they descend from.

features.name: flag field
features.desc-on-touch: Thousands of small flags scatter across the yellowed meadow, each listing a cell's ancestors back five generations. The wind makes them whisper together.

features.name: genealogy pool
features.desc-on-touch: Clear water holds quartz formations, each reflecting a different family's face. You see yourself in the oldest pieces.

features.name: keeper casing
features.desc-on-touch: A eucalyptus node sits in the field, bark riddled with its own growth rings. Inside, a solar cell broadcasts: I am here because here is where I was called to be.

inscription: here each cell knows not only where it came from but why it is becoming

file.name: Apiary_Genealogy_Index_Hand_Annotated.txt
file.note: Three decades of hive records, cross-referenced by blood and by season. Margin notes suggest the beekeeper began to see hives not as separate colonies but as one organism remembering itself.

exits.label: into the field where songs divide by blood
toward cells who learned their own names first
